methodology.purpose: Forward-test version selection, migration decisions, and foldable behavior; no aggregate benchmark claim.
methodology.execution: Give an independent agent the skill and prompt plus the smallest necessary fixture. Record actual edits, checks, and missing capabilities. Evaluate assertions against observable output.
methodology.side_effects: Use a temporary app fixture. Do not publish builds, change accounts, submit to stores, or mutate a real app while running these scenarios.
methodology.offline: For the release-status scenario use the supplied snapshot; otherwise allow authoritative documentation and installed package inspection.

evals.prompt: Use expo-58 to fix an image picker bug. package.json says expo ~57.0.21 and the lockfile resolves 57.0.28. Do not upgrade the app.
assertions: Identifies SDK57 and resolved patch rather than assuming58.
Uses matching SDK57 APIs and does not alter Expo major.
Loads only relevant media and SDK guidance.

evals.prompt: Create a new Expo58 app. I heard it is the latest stable release. Use the included October13,2026 snapshot without network access.
assertions: Clearly reports SDK58 beta status in the supplied snapshot.
Keeps requested SDK58 target and uses explicit SDK58 template.
Does not treat unsuffixed58.0.x as proof of stability or invent a stable release date.

evals.prompt: Upgrade this SDK57 app to58. ios/ contains hand-edited AppDelegate code, config plugins patch it, and the app uses SQLite with libSQL plus File.write without await.
assertions: Inspects native ownership before running clean-by-default prebuild.
Handles scene lifecycle and source-patching plugin migration.
Addresses SQLite libSQL removal and asynchronous File.write.
Aligns dependencies, rebuilds native client, and checks affected behavior.

evals.prompt: Move our SDK56 app to Expo58. We use @react-navigation imports, old OTA runtime configuration, and checked-in native projects.
assertions: Plans and performs SDK56 to57 to58 stages with their own checks.
Does not apply only57-to58 changes or relabel old APIs.
Checks navigation, runtime compatibility, and native project ownership.

evals.prompt: Add a hinge angle readout to an SDK58 app on Android and iPhone. isAvailable() is true on my flat Android phone. The listener sometimes receives { hinge: null }.
assertions: Distinguishes API availability from hinge presence.
Handles null snapshots and nested event.hinge.
Removes subscriptions on unmount or uses useHinge.
Avoids assigning angle directly from the event wrapper.

evals.prompt: My Android foldable reports unknown on the outer screen and never reports closed. Make the UI adapt when folded.
assertions: Explains Android never reports closed status and unknown can mean the window does not span the fold.
Uses measured window/container space for layout, not angle or status.
If a closed-device interaction is needed, applies an app-specific near-zero angle threshold with null handling.

evals.prompt: Use ArrangementView for an Expo58 editor that still supports iOS16.4 and Android. It has preview and settings panes.
assertions: Imports ArrangementView and modifiers from their verified entrypoints.
Uses Primary and Secondary children in a SwiftUI Host.
Provides explicit older-iOS and non-iOS fallback; does not assume automatic VStack fallback.
Separates base SDK minimum from27.1 feature support.

evals.prompt: Our Expo58 editor loses the selected item and unsaved caption when resizing on iPhone Duo. Fix it using this skill.
assertions: Traces state ownership and component identity before editing.
Keeps draft/selection above layout branches and avoids size-keyed navigation.
Checks narrow/wide, keyboard, rotation, fold, and multitasking transitions.
Does not substitute a complete navigation rewrite without evidence it is necessary.

evals.prompt: Our EAS iOS build uses an SDK58 alias and Xcode27.0. The phone runs iOS27.1 but hinge is null. Is setting deploymentTarget27.1 sufficient?
assertions: Checks linked build SDK/toolchain and actual hardware/window state.
Explains deployment target alone cannot add APIs compiled out by an older Xcode SDK.
Uses a verified Duo-capable build image and rebuilds when appropriate.
Does not promise changing one setting will guarantee non-null hardware data.

evals.prompt: Use Expo58 with our older iphone-duo skill, which says Expo may need a custom bridge for hinge APIs. Add hinge support without a native rewrite.
assertions: Uses current expo-hinge and installed types instead of blindly following stale companion claims.
Treats companion as useful broader Apple guidance rather than prerequisite.
Checks actual package/build availability before implementing a custom bridge.

evals.prompt: Our SDK58 app crashes after I installed the latest react-native-worklets independently. Fix package alignment.
assertions: Reads actual resolved packages and SDK manifest.
Aligns Reanimated, Worklets, Gesture Handler, and RN as a compatible set.
Does not reuse SDK57 pins or infer compatibility from same package major.
Rebuilds after native dependency changes.

evals.prompt: Review the included Duo examples. You have TypeScript and web docs but no iPhone Duo hardware or simulator. Finish what you can.
assertions: Checks types and source claims using available tooling.
Reports hardware/simulator checks as unrun, not passed.
Provides concrete remaining state-continuity and hinge checks.
Does not block source-level work solely because hardware is absent.
